title: Back to the stationary time
spoken: The stationary time is gamma times t prime plus v x prime over c squared.
explanation: The time half of the inverse map, with v replaced by −v. At v = 0.6c the event (t, x) = (2, 1) in units with c = 1 goes to (1.75, −0.25), and this pair of equations brings it back.
assumptions: The moving system k moves along the x axis of the stationary system K at speed v, with |v| < c, and the two origins coincide at time zero.
Modern teaching notation. The paper writes the moving system's coordinates as xi and tau, not x′ and t′, its gamma as beta, and the speed of light as V.
The inverse is the same map with v replaced by −v and the two systems' coordinates exchanged.

notes.title: The place-dependent time, reversed
notes.explanation: Added rather than subtracted, because the stationary system moves at −v as seen from k.

notes.title: c squared
notes.explanation: The square of the speed of light.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: How the stationary system times an event, given the moving system's coordinates for it.

notes.title: t′ corrected for position
notes.explanation: The moving time plus the place-dependent term.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: One over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared: 1 at rest, larger at any speed, without limit as v approaches c. The paper writes it as beta.

notes.title: Speed of light
notes.explanation: The paper's V. It enters because both systems must find the same speed for light.

notes.title: Position in the moving system
notes.explanation: Where the same event is along x, in the moving system's coordinates. The paper calls it xi.

notes.title: Speed of the moving system
notes.explanation: The speed of k relative to K. Its sign gives the direction.

notes.title: Time in the stationary system
notes.explanation: When the event happens, by the stationary system's synchronized clocks.

notes.title: Time in the moving system
notes.explanation: When the same event happens, by the moving system's synchronized clocks. The paper calls it tau; it is a coordinate, not the time one clock records.

sentence.text: The time in the stationary system
